scope: Native BoatScript and MotorbikeScript cosmetic hooks; fitted body panels across CarScript, BoatScript and MotorbikeScript
behavior: Server-only choice uses all four persistent-ID parts and the existing vehicle-wrap hash/chance/selected-ID rules.
AfterStoreLoad recomputes the same choice for an unchanged persistent ID and selected settings; no extra save-stream fields.
Per-root synchronized wrap ID; fitted body panels inherit that ID rather than rolling independently.
Client texture application defers after event stacks; 30 attempts per render window; later sync/health/attach can recover.
Persistent-ID readiness retries are bounded at 120 attempts.
Detach and reparent require original owned textures to restore; rejected writes retain ownership for a bounded retry.
Only immediate supported parents and fitted CarDoor/MotorbikePart roots dispatch; no inventory cargo or wheel traversal.
Texture eligibility is controlled by separately audited model/selection mappings.
Server eligibility accepts exact declared slots while the client keeps actual texture-readback guards.
An actually fitted mapped panel can establish vehicle eligibility; late attachments and store loads recheck the cached assembly.
Vehicles with only mapped panels dispatch those panels without retrying an unpaintable body or treating a zero-slot body write as success.

verification.type: Extracted production methods executed through C++ engine adapters with undefined-behavior sanitizer, plus script-root contract checks.
